content: For anyone considering buying this - do not.  It's only marginally better than manual focus, and it IS NOT for continuous autofocus.  the unit "jumps" to each focal point that you've set, so for things like sports or moving the camera, it's completely useless.  The DJI lidar autofocus is continuous and smooth and doesn't require the ridiculous setup this thing requires.  Don't waste your money.

name: CDA_Tek
content: The R1 keys perform different functions depending on time pressed (see Page 18 for details). On the P4K/6K when you are in command mode,it will perform camera functions when Joy L and Joy R are long pressed. Full details of supported functions are on Page 35 and setup of them is in SETUP>MAINTENANCE>BUTTON ASSIGNMENT. A default for the Joy L is the REC function which explains why you are seeing it activate on long presses of the stick. In that menu you can change it for another function.

name: CDA_Tek
content: To recap over the calibration, for the P6K only there are two phases. The first is the Profiling phase  where it ramps the lens from one end to the other in order to calculate the number of steps the lens is capable of. This is dependent on the lens and can range from as few as 30 steps to over 650. All you have to do in this phase as it is automatically incrementing the lens is to press B on the AFX when it reaches the end of travel.

name: CDA_Tek
content: Hi Nate Thank you for supporting the AFX. You are free to mount the AFX where you choose with the only proviso that you must adhere to the position it was in when you calibrated the lens. So, for example, if when you originally calibrated the lens, you had the AFX on an arm 10cm ahead of the shoe mount on your GH5s then it must be in that position when you use it. However, if you do wish to move the AFX position then it is a simple case of making a new calibration with it in that position

name: CDA_Tek
content: Hi There is a simple calibration process. You start at minimum focus,press the A button on the controller which will store the current distance with that focus point.You then move to the next focus point and repeat, then do the next etc The completed calibration is then stored in AFX's internal database and is only performed once per lens AFX then loads the relevant calibration when you change lens (automatically on P4K/6K,from a list for motor only cameras). You can store up to 64 lenses
